# Local-first

## Overview
The "Local-first [IoT](./iot.md)" lunch-and-learn session, hosted at the [Aurora](./aurora-nova-widget-v2.md) office on July 5, featured invited guest presenter Alex Kim from [TeaBuddy](./teabuddy.md). The session explored the philosophy and technical decisions behind [Local-first Software](./local-first-software.md) and architectures for consumer gadgets, highlighting why certain products reject cloud dependencies in favor of local control and direct device communication.

## Key Details
- **Presenter:** Alex Kim (TeaBuddy)
- **Core Topics:**
  - [Bluetooth Low Energy](./bluetooth-low-energy.md) ([BLE](./ble.md)) versus mesh network tradeoffs for consumer [hardware](./hardware.md) gadgets.
  - The reasoning behind TeaBuddy v1's decision to reject cloud accounts entirely in favor of a [local-first](./local-first.md) approach.
  - Live demonstrations comparing a [puck](./teabuddy.md) buzzer against [Nova Widget](./nova-widget.md) LED patterns.
- **Q&A Highlights:**
  - *[Mira](./aurora-nova-widget-v2.md)* noted that mesh network complexity becomes worthwhile when scaling to 6 or more garden [sensors](./sensors.md).
  - *Alex Kim* emphasized user experience, stating that tea drinkers prefer "one device, one job" without unnecessary cloud connectivity.
  - *Jonah* offered to share enclosure supplier contacts.
- **Action Items:**
  - Add a cross-link wiki page for `teabuddy-cross-ref` (noting that it may already exist).
